sols.eventDescription: All systems nominal. Solar panels are generating maximum energy (4 units).
sols.nasaFact: Base coordinates: 18.38°N, 77.58°E (NASA Mars Trek). Background radiation: 384.5 µGy/day (Liulin-MO-CD-Orbit).

sols.eventDescription: A good time to start the greenhouse or water extraction.
sols.nasaFact: Daily radiation dose: 405.4 µGy/day (NASA RadLab, recorded on 2021-05-02).

sols.eventDescription: Wind blew Martian dust onto the solar arrays. Only 3 units of energy are available today!
sols.nasaFact: According to Mars mission data (Mars Trek), dust reduces atmospheric transparency and solar panel efficiency.

sols.eventDescription: Time to check how plants respond to Martian conditions.
sols.nasaFact: NASA OSDR study (OSD-520): cosmic radiation slows down plant growth without shielding.

sols.eventDescription: An M7.6-class solar flare has been detected! A powerful solar storm is approaching.
Dust has reduced energy to 3 units, and the storm is almost here! Reinforce the habitat module in time!
sols.nasaFact: Peak orbital dose before the storm: 656.6 µGy/day (Liulin-MO-AB-Orbit, RadLab).

sols.eventDescription: Peak radiation! Without reinforced hull plating and shields, contamination will spike by +40%!
sols.nasaFact: Real extreme flare from NASA DONKI: X9.0 class (2024-10-03T12:08:00-FLR-001).

kidFriendlyCards.kidTitle: How do plants react to space radiation?
kidFriendlyCards.kidExplanation: NASA experiments showed that without protection, radiation slows down the growth of roots and leaves. That's why crop yield in our greenhouse drops if we ignore radiation levels at the base!

kidFriendlyCards.kidTitle: Why does the crew need thick shielding?
kidFriendlyCards.kidExplanation: According to NASA OSDR medical research, prolonged radiation weakens astronauts' immune defenses. Reinforcing the habitat module keeps the crew healthy.

glossary.definition: A Martian day, lasting 24 hours and 39 minutes.
A powerful explosion on the Sun that releases a stream of dangerous radiation into space.
The measurement of the amount of radiation absorbed by astronauts or instruments.
A layer of loose dust and broken rock covering the surface of Mars.
